land.text: Tannu Uriankhai: 'The end of Qing rule in Tannu Uriankhai came quickly' after the Xinhai Revolution of 10 October 1911; infobox disestablishment December 1911

predecessors.note: Tannu Uriankhai was a Qing frontier governorate; the republic is the Tuvan nobles' state under Governor Oyun Kombu-Dorzhu.

land.text: the republic as a Russian protectorate under the name Uryankhay Krai: 'On 14 April 1914, the Uryankhay Republic became a Russian protectorate as the Uryankhay Krai'

successors.note: The infobox gives 17 April 1914 as the end; the text gives 14 April. The Tannu Uriankhai page dates the protectorate to April 1914 with no day. The Tuvan People's Republic of 1921 is a later state on the same land.

rulers.name: Oyun Kombu-Dorzhu
rulers.title: leader (governor of Tannu Uriankhai)
rulers.note: Infobox 'Leader (1911-1914)'. The Tannu Uriankhai page calls him the governor who 'advocated a Russian protectorate' and then claimed to have been chosen leader of an independent state.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the founding month: Cliopatria begins in 1912 but the infobox gives 'Established: 1 December 1911' ('It was proclaimed as a republic in 1911 by the Tuvan separatist movement and was encouraged by the Russian Empire'). The 1912 outline is used.

148,695 km2, entirely in Russia (89.1-98.9E 49.8-53.6N). Neither page gives an area. The Tannu Uriankhai page says the old territory 'largely' corresponds to modern Tuva, neighbouring Russian areas and 'a small part of Mongolia' (its banners included Khovsgol Nuur), which this shape leaves to Cliopatria's Great Mongol State. 'Tsar Nicholas II ordered Russian troops into the Uryankhay Republic in 1912'; two noyans preferred submission to the Bogd Khanate (undated).

Same outline. A 'Russian-sponsored petition from two Uriankhai khoshuuns in the fall of 1913' asked to be accepted as part of Russia and other khoshuuns followed; the land did not change until April 1914.

correction.text: unchanged outline until the April 1914 protectorate

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row stops after 1913, but the republic lasted to 14 April 1914 ('became a Russian protectorate as the Uryankhay Krai'); the 1913 outline holds for 1914 until the protectorate, after which the russian-empire dossier carries it.

region.text: Tannu Uriankhai, largely the modern Tuva

ledger.note: 1911: the Tuvan nobles proclaim an Uryankhay republic. Infobox 'Established: 1 December 1911' (the day Outer Mongolia declared independence); 'proclaimed as a republic in 1911 by the Tuvan separatist movement and was encouraged by the Russian Empire'. The Tannu Uriankhai page has the end of Qing rule there in December 1911. The page gives no capital and no area.

(infobox: 17 April; Tannu Uriankhai page: 'April 1914 ... formally accepted as a protectorate of Russia'.) The russian-empire dossier should carry the matching gain/vassal_start.

ledger.note: April 1914: the republic ends as a state; the Uryankhay Krai is a Russian protectorate (successor: Uryankhay Krai in the infobox).

wars.outcome: Russian troops entered in 1912 on the pretext of attacks on Russian migrants; two khoshuuns petitioned in fall 1913 to join Russia and the republic became a protectorate on 14 April 1914.
wars.note: No fighting is described; the Bogd Khanate's rival claim (two noyans leaning to Urga, undated) was never backed by troops on the pages opened.

certainty.note: No boundary is described; the banner list (Tannu, Salajik, Tojin, Khovsgol Nuur, Khemchik) is undated.

notes: Both pages are thin on territory: neither gives an area, a capital or a boundary, and the capital list is empty because no page opened names one. The only checks on the Cliopatria shape are the Tannu Uriankhai page's 'largely modern Tuva' and its banner list; Cliopatria's shape sits wholly in Russia, so the Khovsgol Nuur banner and the small Mongolian part were left to Mongolia. The republic is a Russian client from 1912: the russian-empire dossier (eu-17) should carry an occupation/vassal start in 1912 and the protectorate from April 1914 with counterpart republic-of-uryankhay; the great-mongol-state dossier records no Tuva land because the Bogd Khanate never held it on these pages (Bogd page: 'In April 1914, the northern region of Tannu Uriankhai was formally accepted as a Russian protectorate'). The Tuvan People's Republic (1921-1944, annexed by the USSR in 1944 per the Tannu Uriankhai page) is a later state on the same land and needs its own dossier (counterpart in the Soviet group).
